u-mainz.note: The successor medical school lasted until 1822 per the university's own history.

u-vienna-1529-destruction.note: Enrolment collapsed in the late 1520s; by 1529 the theology faculty had only two professors.

u-vienna-1752-reform.note: Van Swieten's medical reform began in 1749; the university became a state institution in 1752 and theology and philosophy were reformed from 1753.

u-vienna-1848-suppression.note: The Aula was the centre of the student revolt and was partly used as barracks from 1848 to 1856.

u-vienna-1849-reform.note: Provisional law of 30 September 1849 and ordinances of 1849–50.

u-heidelberg-1386-founding.note: Papal approval 23 October 1385; formal opening 18 October 1386.

u-heidelberg-1803-refoundation.note: Passed to Baden in 1803; named Ruperto Carola in 1805.

fix.desc: Landgrave Philip I founded the university without papal approval, funded by secularized monasteries; it opened on 30 May 1527 with eleven professors and about 90 students.

u-marburg-1527-founding.note: The university's own history gives the opening as 30 May 1527.

u-cologne-1388-founding.note: Bull of 21 May 1388; opened in 1389 with 21 masters and 737 matriculated students.

u-leipzig-1409-founding.note: Opened on 2 December 1409 with masters and scholars who had come from Prague.

u-wurzburg-1413-destruction.note: Rector Johann Zantfurt was killed in 1413; decline followed from 1415 and the last document of the first university dates from 1427.

u-rostock-1419-founding.note: Papal approval 13 February 1419, opening 12 November 1419; theology faculty approved in 1433.

u-greifswald-1456-founding.note: Bull of Callixtus III dated 29 May 1456; opened 17 October 1456 with Heinrich Rubenow as first rector.

u-freiburg-1457-founding.note: Bull of 20 April 1455; foundation charter 21 September 1457; teaching opened 26 April 1460.

fix.desc: During the conflict over the cathedral chapter (Domfehde) the university left Rostock in March 1487, first for Wismar and then briefly for Lübeck.

u-rostock-1487-relocation.note: The university went first to Wismar, then to Lübeck.

u-leipzig-1543-reform.note: The university library was founded in 1543; the former Dominican friary was formally handed over as the Collegium Paulinum in 1544.

u-dillingen-1553-charter.note: Charles V ratified the privileges; formal inauguration 21 May 1554.

u-jena-1558-founding.note: Hohe Schule opened 1548; imperial privilege signed 15 August 1557; inaugurated 2 February 1558.

u-rostock-1563-confessional.note: Settlement dated 11 May 1563; the university had become Protestant in 1531.

u-dillingen-1564-confessional.note: Some accounts date the handover to the Jesuits to 1563.

u-marburg-1605-confessional.note: The Reformed turn under Landgrave Maurice followed the 1604 succession dispute; Hesse-Darmstadt founded Giessen in 1607.

u-paderborn-1614-founding.note: Founded by Prince-Bishop Dietrich IV von Fürstenberg and entrusted to the Jesuits; imperial and papal privileges followed in 1615.

u-molsheim-1618-founding.note: Dates for university status vary in the literature: 1611, 1618 and 1621 are all given.

u-strasbourg-1621-founding.note: Successor to the school of 1538 and the academy of 1566.

u-rinteln-1621-relocation.note: University status was granted at Stadthagen in 1619/20, and the university moved to Rinteln in 1621.

u-salzburg-1622-founding.note: Formally founded on 8 October 1622 in the presence of Paris Lodron.

u-altdorf-1622-charter.note: Imperial charter dated 3 October 1622; privileges proclaimed in 1623.

u-heidelberg-1622-destruction.note: The Bibliotheca Palatina was taken to Rome in 1623; the university reopened in 1652.

u-marburg-1625-confessional.note: Hesse-Darmstadt took Marburg in 1624; the university returned to Lutheranism and was divided with Kassel by the 1627 settlement.

u-bamberg-1647-founding.note: Founded 14 November 1647; imperial and papal privileges in 1648.

u-greifswald-1648-reform.note: Swedish administration of Western Pomerania began in 1637 and was confirmed by the Peace of Westphalia in 1648.

u-marburg-1653-merger.note: Hesse-Kassel regained Marburg in 1645/46; the 1653 statutes re-established it as a Reformed university.

u-strasbourg-1681-reform.note: The capitulation treaty preserved the Protestant university's autonomy.

u-freiburg-1686-relocation.note: After the French took Freiburg (ceded 1679) most professors and students moved to Konstanz.

u-heidelberg-1693-destruction.note: Heavily hit in the Nine Years' War (1688–97); returned to Heidelberg in 1700.

u-freiburg-1698-relocation.note: Return followed the Peace of Ryswick (1697).

u-breslau-1702-founding.note: Some histories describe the Leopoldina as a Jesuit academy that gained full university status only with the 1811 union.

u-halle-1723-reform.note: Wolff left Halle for Marburg in 1723 and stayed there until 1740.

u-fulda-1734-founding.note: Papal charter 1 July 1732, imperial confirmation 12 March 1733; solemnly inaugurated on 19 September 1733.

u-freiburg-1767-reform.note: Maria Theresa's new curriculum was introduced in 1767 despite much opposition.

u-freiburg-1773-suppression.note: The Jesuit college, church and gymnasium passed to the university in 1777.

u-bamberg-1773-reform.note: Law faculty from 1735, medicine added later; named Universitas Ottoniano-Fridericiana in 1773.

u-graz-1782-reform.note: Joseph II's decree at the end of 1782 turned the university into a lyceum.

u-innsbruck-1782-reform.note: Joseph II reduced the university to a lyceum by decree of 29 November 1781; full teaching resumed in 1792.

u-bonn-electoral-1786-founding.note: The Maxische Akademie of 1777 was raised to a university by imperial patent in 1786.

u-cologne-1798-suppression.note: Teaching was halted in April 1796 under French occupation; the university was formally abolished in 1798.

u-jena-1799-reform.note: Fichte was dismissed in 1799 after the atheism dispute.

u-dillingen-1803-suppression.note: Abolished by Bavarian rescript of 3 November 1803, effective 1804; replaced by a gymnasium and lyceum.

u-fulda-1805-suppression.note: The Benedictines ran it after 1773 and had to close it in 1805, after their monastery was secularized in 1802.

u-erlangen-1810-reform.note: Erlangen passed to Bavaria in 1810 and inherited the assets of Altdorf, closed in 1809.

u-breslau-1811-merger.note: By royal edict of August 1811; five faculties including Catholic and Protestant theology.

u-halle-1813-suppression.note: Closed again by Napoleon's decree of 15 July 1813, reopened after the Battle of Leipzig.

u-munster-1818-reform.note: Law and medicine were closed on 18 October 1818, leaving a two-faculty institution.

u-bonn-1820-reform.note: Arndt was banned from teaching in the wake of the 1819 Carlsbad Decrees; the ban was lifted in 1840.

u-giessen-1824-reform.note: Liebig became professor of chemistry at Giessen in 1824.

u-heidelberg-1900-access.note: Four women enrolled for the summer semester of 1900.

th417.note: Entered 1450, BA 1452, MA and arts faculty member 1457, lectured until leaving for Italy with Bessarion in 1461.

th420.note: Came to Vienna 1745; head of the medical faculty from 1749 until his death in 1772.

th425.note: He held Vienna chairs also 1873–76 and again 1902–06.

th442.note: Matriculated at Cologne in 1425 to study theology; no evidence he taught canon law there.

th538.note: Habilitated at Jena in 1801 and left in March 1807.

th609.note: Honorary professor at Erlangen from 1820 until his move to Munich in 1827.

th450.note: Emeritus in 1897 but continued to head his department until 1902.

th452.note: Discovered X-rays at Würzburg in 1895; moved to Munich in 1900.

th463.note: Called to Rostock in 1550 and lecturing from April 1551 until his death in 1600.

th464.note: Arrived in 1566 and returned home in April 1567; he later revisited Rostock.

th465.note: Chair of mathematics 1624–25 and 1626–28, with a year at Helmstedt in between.

th466.note: Studied and later taught history at Greifswald.

th469.note: Came to Freiburg in June 1502; doctorate in theology in October 1510, then left for Ingolstadt.

th470.note: Ordinarius in civil law from 1506; died in November 1535 (some sources say 1536).

th471.note: Matriculated 1 May 1503; he taught in the theology faculty from 1511 and followed Eck to Ingolstadt in 1512.

th473.note: Held the Freiburg chair of economics from 1894 until he moved to Heidelberg in 1897.

th476.note: Came to Ingolstadt in late 1519; professor of Hebrew and Greek from 1520; left because of plague in 1521.

th478.note: Taught mathematics and Hebrew at Ingolstadt from about 1610.

th479.note: Extraordinary professor from 1772, chair of canon law from 1773; dismissed in 1785 after the ban on the Illuminati.

th484.note: Professor of moral theology at Trier from 1632, of biblical studies from 1634, until his death in 1635.

th485.note: Regular teaching was interrupted by the French occupation of 1792; he resigned in 1797.

th486.note: Professor of theology from 1484, probably until about 1491; he died in Tübingen at the end of 1495.

th489.note: His death in 1631 left the Tübingen chair of mathematics vacant.

th497.note: At Wittenberg from 1504/05 (doctorate 1510); became pastor at Orlamünde in late 1523 and lost his Wittenberg post in 1524.

th506.note: Matriculated at Frankfurt (Oder) in 1512, after Leipzig (1506).

th514.note: Studied at Marburg from 1795, doctorate 1800, then lecturer and from 1803 professor until he left for Landshut in 1808.

th522.note: Entered at sixteen (about 1746) and left without a degree.

th578.note: Taught law at Halle from 1690, before its formal inauguration in 1694, until his death in 1728.

th583.note: Professor at Halle from 1783 until Napoleon closed the university in 1806; he moved to Berlin in April 1807.

th587.note: Professor of physiology from January 1823 until his return to Prague in 1850.

th588.note: University librarian from 1823; professor from 1830 (full professor 1835) until his dismissal in 1842.

th589.note: Studied philosophy and history at Breslau and Berlin, 1843–46.

th592.note: Privatdozent from 1850, full professor from 1872; died in Breslau in 1898.

th594.note: Enrolled 1763; professor from 1770 (full professor 1775) until his death in 1799.

th598.note: Studied 1795–98; director of the observatory from 1807 until his death in 1855.

th603.note: Enrolled 1832 and moved to Berlin in September 1833.
